<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide to producing a comprehensive system‐design diagram for RSS-Bridge, tailored to the project’s purpose and structure.

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose  
   • Type: PHP web application, implemented as a single‐page “front controller” that dynamically generates RSS/Atom/JSON/etc. feeds for target websites.  
   • Purpose: Scrape or fetch content from sites without feeds, normalize it into a standard feed format, and serve it via HTTP.  

2. Analyze the File Structure  
   • Dev & Ops  
     – .devcontainer, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, GitHub Actions workflows → development and CI/CD environment.  
   • Entry Point  
     – index.php → bootstraps the framework; loads dependencies and dispatches to actions.  
   • Core Libraries  
     – lib/ → core classes (BridgeAbstract, CacheFactory, FormatFactory, Container, FeedParser, etc.).  
   • Actions (Controllers)  
     – actions/ → one class per action (DisplayAction, FindfeedAction, HealthAction, etc.) implementing ActionInterface.  
   • Bridges (Adapters)  
     – bridges/ → ~450+ Bridge classes inheriting BridgeAbstract, each encapsulating logic to fetch & parse a specific site.  
   • Formats  
     – formats/ → output serializers (AtomFormat, JsonFormat, HtmlFormat, MrssFormat, PlaintextFormat, SfeedFormat).  
   • Caching  
     – caches/ → implementations of CacheInterface (FileCache, SQLiteCache, MemcachedCache, ArrayCache, NullCache).  
   • Middleware  
     – middlewares/ → Chain-of-Responsibility (BasicAuth, TokenAuth, CacheMiddleware, ExceptionMiddleware, MaintenanceMiddleware, SecurityMiddleware).  
   • Static Assets & Templates  
     – static/, templates/ → UI assets and PHP-view templates for HTML responses.  
   • Tests & Documentation  
     – tests/, docs/ → unit tests and developer/user guides.

3. Examine the README for Additional Insights  
   • Runtime stack: PHP ≥7.4, typically served by nginx + php-fpm or Docker.  
   • Deployment options: plain PHP server, Nginx, Docker, Composer, Heroku, Scalingo, etc.  
   • Third-party libs: Parsedown (markdown), Simple HTML DOM, php-urljoin, PSR-like patterns.

4. Creating the System-Design Diagram  
   a. Main Components  
     1. Web Server Layer  
        – nginx or built-in PHP server (serves static files and proxies dynamic requests to PHP‐FPM).  
     2. Front Controller (index.php)  
        – bootstraps DI container, registers routes/actions.  
     3. Middleware Chain  
        – authentication, rate limits, caching check, exception handling, maintenance mode.  
     4. Action Router & Controllers  
        – picks an Action class (e.g. DisplayAction) based on request parameters.  
     5. Bridge Façade  
        – BridgeFactory instantiates a specific Bridge (e.g. RedditBridge), BridgeAbstract.collectData() fetches/parses external site.  
     6. Data Store / Cache Layer  
        – CacheMiddleware & CacheInterface implementations to persist feed results (filesystem, SQLite, memcached).  
     7. Format Layer  
        – FormatFactory wraps feed items into Atom/JSON/HTML/MRSS/etc.  
     8. HTTP Response  
        – formatted payload returned through PHP-FPM to client.  
     9. External Services  
        – target websites’ HTML pages or APIs being scraped by Bridge classes.  

   b. Relationships and Data Flow  
     – Draw a directional flow: Client → Web Server → PHP Front Controller → Middleware Chain → Action → Bridge → External Site → Bridge returns items → Cache → Format → Response → Client.  

   c. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
     – Front Controller (centralized entry point)  
     – Chain of Responsibility (middleware pipeline)  
     – Factory Pattern (BridgeFactory, FormatFactory, CacheFactory)  
     – Dependency Injection (Container wiring lib/dependencies.php)  
     – Adapter Pattern (Bridge classes encapsulate vendor-specific scraping logic)  

   d. Key Technologies & Libraries  
     – PHP 7.4+, PSR-style code organization  
     – nginx + php-fpm or Docker  
     – Parsedown, Simple HTML DOM, php-urljoin  
     – PHPUnit for testing, PHPCS for linting  

5. Tailoring the Diagram to This Project  
   • Focus on extensibility points: Bridges folder (plug-in adapters) and CacheFactory (pluggable backends).  
   • Emphasize HTTP request handling vs. static asset serving (static/ vs. index.php).  
   • Show how config files (config.default.ini.php, config.ini.php) influence cache/auth settings.  

6. Diagram Guidelines  
   • Use distinct shapes/colors for:  
     – Web Server & PHP Runtime (e.g. grey box)  
     – Core Framework Components (index.php, Middlewares, Container) in one color (blue)  
     – Action & Bridge Layers (green)  
     – Cache Layer (orange)  
     – Format Layer (purple)  
     – External Sites (cloud icons)  
   • Label each component clearly (e.g., “CacheMiddleware”, “RedditBridge”, “JsonFormat”).  
   • Use directional arrows to show data/request flow.  
   • Annotate key interactions (e.g., “Cache miss? → Bridge.collectData()”).

7. Essential Details to Capture  
   • The front controller’s role in wiring together container, middleware, router, and action classes.  
   • The middleware pipeline’s entry/exit points (authentication, caching, error handling).  
   • The interplay between Bridge implementations and Cache backends.  
   • The pluggable nature of Format implementations.  
   • External dependencies (static files, third-party libs, external websites).

By following these steps and layering your diagram from web server down to individual Bridge and Format components, you will produce a detailed, accurate architecture view of RSS-Bridge that highlights its extensibility, caching strategy, and request-processing pipeline.
